title: Applying DFT to Organic Chemistry – Part A

quiz.q: Staggered ethane is more stable than eclipsed ethane. For the reaction staggered → eclipsed, ΔE = Σ νᵢEᵢ = (+1)·E(eclipsed) + (−1)·E(staggered) is…
options: zero, because it is the same molecule
quiz.explain: The product (eclipsed) is higher in energy, so ΔE > 0. Here that ΔE is the rotational barrier. Always keep track of the reaction direction when you compute signed errors.

quiz.q: Which of these functionals is a **meta-GGA** (no exact exchange)?
quiz.explain: SCAN depends on the density, its gradient and the kinetic-energy density (meta-GGA rung). PBE is a GGA, and B3LYP and PBE0 are hybrid GGAs.

quiz.q: What does the “-D4” suffix add to a functional?
options: Four extra diffuse basis functions per atom
A pairwise (plus three-body) dispersion energy correction that depends on the geometry and on atomic charges
quiz.explain: Grimme’s D4 model adds a London-dispersion correction computed from the geometry, with C₆ coefficients that depend on coordination numbers and atomic partial charges. It doesn’t change the density or the basis.

quiz.q: Why do we divide the total job time by the number of SCF cycles?
options: To compare the cost of one iteration, independent of how hard it was to converge
Because Q-Chem reports time per cycle in the wrong units
To correct for the number of basis functions
Because hybrid functionals need fewer cycles
quiz.explain: Different functionals converge in different numbers of cycles. Time per cycle isolates the intrinsic cost of the functional, for example the exact-exchange (K) build in hybrids or the nonlocal VV10 term.
